haiku-low.q1: Keys load at startup before the HTTP server accepts requests. /healthz returns 200 only when all three keys are loaded, so traffic arrives only after loading.
haiku-low.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then logs names and error class and exits non-zero. The rollout halts and old pods keep serving, since maxUnavailable is 0.
haiku-low.q3: Every 5 minutes with jitter, it re-reads each secret and swaps in a changed value. If a read fails or is malformed, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning, and retries at the next interval.
haiku-low.q4: Key values are held in process memory only. They must never appear in logs, disk, environment variables, or caches, and core dumps are disabled.
haiku-low.q5: The orders-api-prod identity has read-only access to prod secrets and engineers are denied prod reads. Only the security on-call group can write prod secrets.
haiku-low.q6: Keys remain in git history and in old images, so removing them from the yaml does not erase them. Revoking the old keys at the providers makes them harmless.
haiku-low.q7: Clients call secrets.get(name) on each request. It returns the current in-memory value without network access, and requests in progress keep the key they already read.
haiku-low.q8: Every pod's reported version ids on /healthz must match the step 2 version ids. Old key last-used times must show no use for at least 10 minutes, and unexplained service use blocks revocation.
haiku-low.q9: Set store access, then copy keys into the store, then switch the app to read from the store and remove yaml keys in the same PR, then revoke old provider keys.
haiku-low.q10: make run uses APP_ENV=dev and config/app.dev.yaml, reading orders-api/dev/* with the engineer's own identity. make run-offline uses in-memory fake keys, allowed only when APP_ENV=local.
haiku-low.q11: Startup needs all three keys, so the missing secret's read is retried 3 times, then the instance logs and exits non-zero. It never starts with partial keys. The document does not address this case explicitly.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded (all three, from the store) before the HTTP server starts accepting requests; /healthz returns 200 only when all three are loaded, so ready comes after loading.
sonnet.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart (up to 4 attempts), then logs secret names and error class and exits non-zero. It never becomes ready, the rollout halts (maxUnavailable 0), and the old pods keep serving traffic, so customers are unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A timer re-reads every secret from the store every 5 minutes (with jitter). If the version id changed, the new value is swapped into the in-memory object in one step under a lock. If a read fails or returns empty/malformed, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning (name, error class, current version id), and tries again at the next interval; no retry loop, each secret handled separately.
sonnet.q4: Held in process memory only, in one in-memory object with their version ids. They must never appear on disk (no disk cache), in environment variables, in logs, tickets, chat, shell history, CI variables or files. Version ids may be logged.
sonnet.q5: Read: orders-api-prod service identity (read-only on orders-api/prod/*); engineers have no prod access. Write: only the security on-call group.
sonnet.q6: Git history is not rewritten and old images in the registry still contain the keys, so the old values remain visible. They are harmless because they are revoked at the providers in step 8 (and old images are marked do-not-deploy or deleted in step 9).
sonnet.q7: Clients no longer copy the key in __init__; on each call they invoke secrets.get("<name>"), which returns the current value from memory without touching the network. A request in progress keeps the key it already read.
sonnet.q8: Query each of the 4 pods for the version ids it reports (exposed on /healthz) and compare with the version ids from step 2. Also wait at least 10 minutes after the last old pod stopped, then check each provider console that the old key has had no use since, and look for other users of old keys. Confirmation rests on reported version ids, not elapsed time.
sonnet.q9: 1) Set up store access/policies (and paths); 2) create new keys at providers and write them to the store (old stay valid); 3) merge code (switch app to read from store and remove api_key lines from the yaml, in one PR); 4) preflight; 5) deploy; 6) confirm; 7) local dev cutover (parallel with 5-6); 8) revoke old provider keys; 9) cleanup. Removal from the committed file happens with the code switch in step 3.
sonnet.q10: From the dev store paths orders-api/dev/* (make run, APP_ENV=dev), read with the engineer's own identity; or from in-memory fake keys with make run-offline (APP_ENV=local only).
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED explicitly. The document says that if any read fails it retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero; it does not specifically describe a missing secret.
sonnet.q12: Undecided. Security has not decided whether or how often to rotate on a schedule; the plan picks no cadence (open question).
